headline: Congress passed a resolution that cancels a Labor Department rule about state-run retirement savings programs for private-sector workers.
what_it_does: The Department of Labor had issued a rule explaining when state payroll savings programs with automatic enrollment would not count as employer pension plans under ERISA, a federal law. This joint resolution overturns that rule, so it no longer applies. The official summary does not describe any replacement rule or other changes to state programs.

who_it_affects.group: States that were setting up or planning automatic payroll savings programs for private-sector workers
who_it_affects.how: The federal guidance they had been given on designing these programs no longer applies.

who_it_affects.group: Private-sector employers that might be covered by state savings programs
who_it_affects.how: The rule that described how these programs would be treated under federal pension law was canceled, which changes the guidance they could rely on.

who_it_affects.group: Private-sector workers whose employers do not offer a retirement plan
who_it_affects.how: The resolution removes the federal rule that had been intended to guide state programs that could give them a way to save for retirement through payroll deduction.
